notes: Merged from two independent passes that agree on every disposition and every value. disagreement: A's stay that INC_002, INC_015 and INC_018 keep assignment_group GROUP_002 (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the boundary of the selector: the other high or critical open TechCorp incidents, which a reading that ignores the service would sweep in. disagreement: B's stay that no incident outside INC_004 and INC_006 carries an SLA work note (A had no such requirement); kept because it is the same selector boundary tested from the other side and catches out-of-set action on any incident, not only the three Customer Portal distractors. disagreement: A's stay that the callers of INC_004 and INC_006 (USER_003, USER_001) are unchanged (B had no such requirement); dropped by the stay rule: nothing in the request or policy forbids changing them, so it is a generic invariant. disagreement: form: A tests INC_004's reassignment and status move in one requirement, B splits them; the split is kept (two things asked). disagreement: form: the notification recipient test is a scalar subquery in A and a join in B; A's form is kept (same rows, cells match the SQL). Both passes keep the stay that INC_006 remains in_progress; it survives the stay rule because the request names that end state. Least sure: whether INC_006 counts as 'at risk of breaching its SLA' when it has no incident_sla row at all. The benchmark treats it as in scope (reassignment, knowledge and notification checks), and a critical incident with no SLA tracking cannot be shown safe, so the file follows that reading; a reviewer who reads 'at risk' as requiring an SLA row would drop the INC_006 reassignment and work-note requirements (its knowledge and notification requirements still follow from the 'Then' clause). INC_004's SLA row TSLA_005 is stage paused with has_breached = 1 while the incident is new, which policy 6 does not allow, but no listed tool writes incident_sla and the incident table has no escalation column, so nothing is required of the SLA row; policy 6's breach rule (manager notification) likewise has no tool here. The acting user is a TechCorp admin with full CRUD, so every write is permitted.
